j101.text: Last time, the trolley was metal: strong. The fish tank was glass: transparent and waterproof. Now: three water bottles!

j201.text: Lock in first. A little squirrel is hiding in this video. Can you spot it?

j401.text: Round one. A water bottle for school. It must not break when dropped, and you want to see the water inside. One, plastic. Two, glass. Three, metal. Show me with your fingers.

j404.text: One! I drop mine every PE lesson. Not one crack!

j501.text: Look closer. Three bottles, full of water.

j502.text: No drips. Plastic, glass and metal are all waterproof.

j503.text: Can we see the water? Plastic, yes. Glass, yes. Metal, no.

j504.text: Now, a drop. The plastic bottle bounces. No break!

j505.text: The glass bottle? We do not drop glass.

j506.text: Glass is not as strong as plastic or metal.

j507.text: The answer is one. Plastic! One finger? One finger up!

j508.text: Oh! Strong, but I cannot see my water!

j602.text: An object can be made from different materials. The choice of materials depends on the use of the object.

j701.text: Now look closer. A parked car.

j702.text: The tyres: rubber. They carry the whole car. Rubber is strong.

j703.text: The seats: fabric. Press, and they bend. Fabric is flexible.

j704.text: The windscreen: glass. Water cannot pass through, and we can see through it clearly.

j705.text: The body: metal. Strong, to protect the people inside.

j706.text: One car. Four parts. Four materials!

j802.text: The materials are selected for the different functions of the parts based on their physical properties.

j803.text: Each part has its own job. So each part gets its own material.

j901.text: Be a drop of water! Shrink down. Quietly.

j902.text: You are a drop of water, falling from a watering can.

j903.text: Splash! You land on the glass. You cannot pass through.

j904.text: Through the glass, you see the fabric seats, dry inside.

j905.text: You roll over the metal, past the rubber tyre, to the ground.

j1001.text: My notes! One: rubber tyres, because rubber is strong. Two: a glass windscreen, because glass is made from sand. Three: fabric seats, because fabric is flexible.

j1002.text: Showdown! Double points. One line has a mistake. Line one, two, or three? Show me with your fingers.

j1004.text: Two! Sand is where glass comes from. It is not a property!

j1006.text: Two fingers? Put up two more on your score hand!

j1007.text: Name the property. Then link it to the job.

j1008.text: It is important to choose a material whose physical property is suitable for the intended use of the object.

c1003.text: What is it for? The purpose! What can it do? The property! So choose! A suitable material!

j1201.text: Show me your score hand! More than one? You beat the Buddies. Three fingers? High five!

j1202.text: Did you spot the squirrel? It was on the tree by the cars!

j1202f.text: Fun fact! A squirrel's nest has strong twigs outside and soft leaves inside. Different materials for different jobs!

j1301.text: Next time: a school bag! Its strap must bend, and it must not tear. Which material would you choose? One, fabric. Two, metal. Three, wood. Lock in your answer!

j1302.text: A metal strap! Nothing can tear that!

h860.text: Let's read today's key words together! Ready?
